points.title: 早期教育
points.description: 1608年12月9日，约翰·弥尔顿出生于伦敦一个富裕的公证人家庭。他从小接受严格的教育，在家乡的圣保罗学校学习，展现出非凡的文学天赋。这一时期，他开始接触古典文学，特别是荷马、维吉尔和奥维德的作品，为他后来的创作奠定了坚实基础。他的父亲是一名音乐家，这使弥尔顿从小也受到音乐熏陶，影响了他的诗歌节奏感。
points.descriptionEn: Born on December 9, 1608, in London to a wealthy notary family, John Milton received rigorous education from an early age. At St. Paul's School, he displayed exceptional literary talent and began studying classical literature, particularly the works of Homer, Virgil, and Ovid, which laid the foundation for his later writings. His father was a musician, which influenced Milton's poetic sense of rhythm throughout his life.

points.title: 剑桥求学
points.description: 1625年，弥尔顿进入剑桥大学基督学院学习。在这里，他勤奋学习古典语言和文学，创作了大量拉丁文和希腊文诗歌。1632年，他获得硕士学位后离开剑桥。在剑桥期间，他开始创作早期英语诗歌，如《科马斯》和《利西达斯》，展现了他对政治和宗教问题的关注。这段学术经历培养了他深厚的古典学识和严谨的学术态度，为他后来的政治和宗教论著打下了基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1625, Milton entered Christ's College, Cambridge, where he studied classical languages and literature diligently, composing numerous poems in Latin and Greek. After receiving his master's degree in 1632, he left Cambridge. During his time there, he began writing early English poems such as 'Comus' and 'Lycidas', showing his growing interest in political and religious issues. This academic period cultivated his profound classical knowledge and rigorous scholarly approach, forming the foundation for his later political and religious writings.

points.title: 欧洲游学
points.description: 1638年至1639年，弥尔顿进行了为期15个月的欧洲大陆游学，访问了法国、意大利等地。在巴黎，他会见了著名学者雨果·格罗提乌斯；在佛罗伦萨，他见到了伽利略，这位科学家的遭遇让他对宗教自由有了更深的思考。这次游学使弥尔顿接触到欧洲大陆的先进思想和艺术，拓宽了他的视野。然而，随着英国国内政治局势的变化，他决定提前结束游学，返回英国投身于日益激烈的宗教和政治论战。
points.descriptionEn: From 1638 to 1639, Milton embarked on a 15-month tour of the European continent, visiting France and Italy. In Paris, he met the renowned scholar Hugo Grotius; in Florence, he encountered Galileo, whose situation deepened Milton's thinking on religious freedom. This journey exposed him to advanced continental ideas and art, broadening his perspective. However, as political tensions in England escalated, he decided to cut his journey short and return to England to engage in the increasingly fierce religious and political debates.

points.title: 政治活动
points.description: 1640年，英国革命爆发，弥尔顿积极投身政治活动，成为议会派的重要支持者。1649年，查理一世被处决后，弥尔顿被任命为共和国拉丁文秘书，负责撰写外交文件和宣传材料。这一时期，他创作了大量政治和宗教论著，包括《为英国人民辩护》、《再辩护》和《论出版自由》等，为共和政体辩护。1652年，他因过度劳累导致视力严重下降，最终完全失明。尽管如此，他仍坚持工作，口授完成了许多重要作品。1660年王政复辟后，他一度面临被捕的危险，但在朋友帮助下得以幸免。
points.descriptionEn: With the outbreak of the English Revolution in 1640, Milton actively engaged in politics, becoming a prominent supporter of the parliamentary cause. After Charles I's execution in 1649, Milton was appointed Secretary for Foreign Tongues to the Commonwealth, responsible for writing diplomatic documents and propaganda. During this period, he produced numerous political and religious works, including 'The Tenure of Kings and Magistrates', 'Defensio Secunda', and 'Areopagitica', defending the republican government. By 1652, his eyesight severely deteriorated due to overwork, eventually leading to complete blindness. Despite this, he continued working, dictating many important works. After the Restoration in 1660, he faced the risk of arrest but was spared through the help of influential friends.

points.title: 史诗创作
points.description: 1667年，弥尔顿出版了史诗《失乐园》，这部作品以人类堕落的故事为主题，展现了他对神学、政治和道德的深刻思考。1671年，他又相继出版了《复乐园》和《斗士参孙》。这些作品创作于他完全失明之后，由他口授，助手记录完成。《失乐园》被认为是英语文学史上最伟大的史诗之一，对后世文学产生了深远影响。这一时期，尽管健康状况恶化，弥尔顿仍坚持创作，完成了他一生中最重要的文学成就，确立了他在英国文学史上的崇高地位。
points.descriptionEn: In 1667, Milton published the epic poem 'Paradise Lost', which tells the story of humanity's fall and demonstrates his profound thoughts on theology, politics, and morality. In 1671, he followed with 'Paradise Regained' and 'Samson Agonistes'. These works were created after his complete blindness, dictated by Milton and recorded by assistants. 'Paradise Lost' is considered one of the greatest epics in English literary history, exerting profound influence on later literature. Despite deteriorating health, Milton persisted in his creative work, completing his most significant literary achievements and securing his esteemed position in English literary history.

points.title: 晚年与逝世
points.description: 1674年11月8日，约翰·弥尔顿在伦敦逝世，享年65岁。他的晚年生活相对平静，但仍受到健康问题的困扰。在生命的最后阶段，他修订了《失乐园》的第二版，并继续关注政治和宗教问题。弥尔顿的葬礼在圣吉尔斯教堂举行，他被安葬在教堂墓地。尽管他生前经历了政治动荡和个人苦难，但他的文学成就和思想遗产对后世产生了深远影响。他的作品不仅体现了文艺复兴时期的人文主义精神，也反映了英国革命时期的政治理想，成为英国文学和思想史上的重要遗产。
points.descriptionEn: On November 8, 1674, John Milton died in London at the age of 65. His later years were relatively peaceful but marked by health issues. In his final months, he revised the second edition of 'Paradise Lost' and continued to follow political and religious developments. Milton's funeral was held at St Giles Church, where he was buried in the churchyard. Despite experiencing political turmoil and personal suffering during his lifetime, his literary achievements and intellectual legacy have had a profound impact on subsequent generations. His works not only embody the humanist spirit of the Renaissance but also reflect the political ideals of the English Revolution, becoming an important legacy in English literary and intellectual history.

supporter.zh: 弥尔顿被赞誉为英国文学史上最伟大的诗人之一，他的《失乐园》被誉为英语文学的巅峰之作。支持者认为他是一位坚定的自由斗士，为言论自由和共和政体辩护，其《论出版自由》成为现代自由主义思想的基石。他的作品融合了古典文学传统与基督教神学，展现了人类尊严与自由的崇高价值。弥尔顿在失明后仍坚持创作，体现了非凡的意志力和对艺术的执着追求，成为后世艺术家和思想家的精神楷模。
supporter.en: Milton is celebrated as one of the greatest poets in English literary history, with 'Paradise Lost' regarded as a pinnacle of English literature. Supporters view him as a steadfast champion of liberty, defending freedom of speech and republican government in works like 'Areopagitica', which became a cornerstone of modern liberal thought. His works blend classical literary traditions with Christian theology, embodying the sublime values of human dignity and freedom. Milton's perseverance in creating despite blindness demonstrates extraordinary willpower and artistic dedication, making him a spiritual model for later artists and thinkers.

critic.zh: 批评者指出弥尔顿的政治立场存在矛盾，他一方面支持议会革命，另一方面却拥护清教主义严格道德观，甚至支持审查制度。他的神学观点也受到质疑，特别是对三位一体教义的质疑使他被一些基督教团体视为异端。此外，他的诗歌风格被认为过于冗长和复杂，现代读者往往难以完全欣赏。在政治方面，他被批评为过于理想化，对现实政治的复杂性认识不足，导致其政治理想最终未能实现。
critic.en: Critics point out contradictions in Milton's political stance—he supported parliamentary revolution while advocating Puritan moral strictness and even censorship. His theological views were also questioned, particularly his doubts about the Trinity doctrine, which led some Christian groups to view him as a heretic. Additionally, his poetic style is often considered overly lengthy and complex, making it difficult for modern readers to fully appreciate. Politically, he is criticized for being too idealistic and underestimating the complexities of real-world politics, resulting in the failure of his political ideals.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，弥尔顿被定位为连接文艺复兴与启蒙时代的桥梁人物。他的作品既体现了古典人文主义传统，又预示了现代个人主义和自由思想的兴起。作为英国革命时期的政治思想家，他的共和理念影响了后世民主理论的发展。在文学领域，他的史诗创作影响了浪漫主义诗人，特别是华兹华斯和拜伦。流行文化中，他的形象常与知识分子的抗争精神联系在一起，成为抵抗压迫、追求自由的象征。弥尔顿的生平和作品展现了个人如何在政治动荡中坚持艺术创作和思想探索的典范。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Milton is positioned as a bridge figure connecting the Renaissance and the Enlightenment. His works embody both classical humanist traditions and foreshadow the rise of modern individualism and liberal thought. As a political thinker during the English Revolution, his republican ideals influenced the development of later democratic theories. In literature, his epic poetry influenced Romantic poets, particularly Wordsworth and Byron. In popular culture, his image is often associated with the spirit of intellectual resistance, becoming a symbol of opposition to oppression and the pursuit of freedom. Milton's life and work exemplify how individuals can maintain artistic creation and intellectual inquiry amidst political turmoil.

self.zh: 宁可在自己的土地上受穷，也不在别人的富饶土地上为王。
self.en: Better to reign in hell than serve in heaven.

others.zh: 弥尔顿是英语文学中最伟大的风格大师，他的语言庄严而崇高，思想深刻而富有诗意。
others.en: Milton is the greatest master of style in English literature; his language is majestic and sublime, his thoughts profound and poetic.
